text:
alex: Heads up — profiler (long-context L4 tests) shows steady RSS growth over ~30m, not accounted for by inflight KV entries. I think allocator fragmentation is leaving lots of small unusable holes. attaching quick pprof snippet.

maya: Got it. quick look: large number of live segments in 'kv_block_alloc' and a very high fragmentation ratio reported by our tracer. Sample: 
```
heap_objects: 124k
kv_block_total: 62k
kv_block_free: 18k
avg_block_size: 3.8k
fragmentation_ratio: 1.86
largest_contiguous_free: 24MB
```
Looks like many small blocks pinned by cold references.

jin: Is this the same pattern as the slot-churn bursts? different: churn spikes were transient. This is steady growth during long generation sessions (8k-32k steps) where many tiny tail allocations never get reused.

alex: Exactly. Hypothesis: allocator's 4KB base size + rigid buddy rounding means lots of 4KB fragments for tail kv entries; compaction doesn't trigger because free percentage per slab never crosses the global threshold.

sam: Quick mitigation ideas: increase base block size for tail allocations to 8KB (cut fragmentation), or implement periodic hole-coalescing that runs off the hot path and compacts if free_ratio>12%. Which is less invasive?

maya: 8KB bump is the smallest change but may regress throughput for tiny short-context requests (more wasted memory per small entry). Compactor is more complex but more flexible: we can target slabs with high internal fragmentation and perform in-place copy-out + free (requires pause windows).

jin: What about an opportunistic compaction that runs only on idle GPUs (util<15%) and only for slabs with fragmentation_ratio>1.5? That avoids latency impact. We can add metrics: slab_frag_ratio and slab_free_fragment_count.

alex: I prototyped an opportunistic compactor yesterday. Flag: `--kv-compactor-enable=true` `--kv-compact-thresh=0.12` `--kv-compactor-idle-util=0.15`. Basic approach: select candidate slab, allocate contiguous staging chunk, migrate live kv segments to staging, free old slab holes, then return staging as new slab region. Works but observed a transient CPU spike and a ~60ms tail latency hiccup during migration on our older test rigs.

maya: Can we stagger chunk moves (micro-move) to keep worst-case bounded? move N entries per tick (N=64) and observe tail lat. Also telemetry for live-copy bandwidth.

sam: Agree. Also run A/B with 8KB base vs compactor. We'll measure memory growth over 2-hour long-context sessions and tail-latency 95/99.

jin: I'll open an experimental branch with both toggles + sampler for slab candidate selection. PR will include perf harness. Plan: canary rollout on 3 dedicated hosts (night window).

ops-bot: deploy-schedule created: canary group = eng-runtime-canary-3, window = 02:00-04:00 UTC, rollback-on-error=true.

alex: Thanks — let's keep this thread for quick sync. If compactor A/B looks good we should land compactor behind feature flag and ship base-size bump as fallback.

maya: One more note: storage format minor change required (kv header alignment) — jin pls add compatibility tests.

jin: on it, will attach perf graphs in PR and raw pprof snapshots.

sam: tagging @maya @alex for visibility, will triage results tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:

alex: observed initial canary memory curve flattening on one host after compactor enabled (small early win). keep monitoring.
